[the rule's own record before the fold]
PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB256, 2026-09-13). The scanner itself was SUSTAINED by the refutation ('NvScan is faithful and the leg b/c discriminator at line 621 is right'); all three grounds of the PARTIAL were about EVIDENCE and about one incorporated half, and each is now discharged on its own terms.
(1) THE INCORPORATED §15.67.3 r4 STANDARD-BINARY HALF is the PB198 decline, recorded per-row and NOT by widening inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only selector (which takes only rules conditioned SOLELY on the mode — this one is not). Annex A.3 item 2 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY processor-dependent and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support plus the duty to warn at compile time and document the absence; docs/CONFORMANCE.md §1/§2 carries the documentation and conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/standard-binary-test-numval-2014 proves the decline ON THIS FUNCTION'S OWN PATH rather than on the OPTIONS clause in isolation. ArithmeticModes.NumvalDigitCap records the 35 anyway, so the table has no hole and the lane cannot quietly answer a question it was never asked. This is the disposition PB258's GR-14.9.12.4-1 / -7 took for the identical shape.
(2) THE LEG-c WIDTH EVIDENCE is replaced, as the refuter asked: golden N10's verdict of 32 is 32 for any width >= 32 and measured nothing about width. conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_leg_c_and_national now measures leg c) over a DATA ITEM directly and over a NATIONAL one — SP (PIC X(4) all spaces) = 5 and NS (PIC N(4) all spaces) = 5 with LEN pinning FUNCTION LENGTH(NSP) = 4 in the same run, so 'FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1' is OBSERVED, both operands of it, rather than inferred from CobolString.Fit.
(3) THE COMPILER ARM OF §15.67.3 r5 IS NOW MEASURED END TO END, which is the whole point of this note. conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_mode_flags carries three compilation units — no clause / DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA / OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD — and asserts each flag in BOTH directions on TEST-NUMVAL itself: P1 "1.5"=0 and P2 "1,5"=2 without the clause, D1 "1,5"=0 and D2 "1.5"=2 with it, so ctx.Data.DecimalPointIsComma -> IntrinsicRenderer.CommaFlag -> the emitted named argument is exercised rather than a literal. The mirror pair is what makes it discriminating: a dead arm passes either half alone.
THE NATIONAL ALTERNATIVE of §15.93.3 r1, flagged unmeasured in BOTH directions, is now measured in both: NA (PIC N(8) "123.45  ") = 0, NC (N"123cr") = 0 for §15.67.3 r1's national CR bullet, NL (the national LITERAL form) = 0, and NB (N"12 34") = 4 — a verdict that also proves positions are counted in NATIONAL CHARACTER POSITIONS, since a byte-counted image would answer 7.
EDITION GATE: conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/test_validators_below_2002 now names TEST-NUMVAL-F beside its three siblings (COBOL1502 at 85), so the whole quartet's window is pinned.
STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: the two-formats-are-ALTERNATIVES discipline, the r2 leading-space handling, the leg b/c discriminator, and the digit-cap sub-notes adjudicated on their own rows.

[folded RV-15.93.4-L2.1 = §15.93.4 1) b) 1.: CONFORMS]
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.4 "If argument-1 is '0 1', the returned value will be 3." -> OK (§15.93.4 rule 1, sub-note 1 under leg b). READ: NvScan (Exact.cs:603-637). The sub-note has TWO halves and both are in the code. (i) "one or more spaces following one or more digits is valid" — after the digit loop breaks, line 622 skips the space run WITHOUT reporting it, and if the string ends there (line 637, i == n) the verdict is 0; a trailing sign or CR/DB may legally follow the skipped spaces (line 630-633), so "0 " and "0 -" and "12 CR" all return 0. (ii) "the returned value is the position of the first non-space character following the spaces" — the fall-through at line 634 returns i + 1 where i is the index reached AFTER the space run was skipped, i.e. the first non-space, not the first space. Hand-traced against the standard's own example: "0 1" -> digit '0' consumed (i=0), loop breaks on the space (i=1), anyDigit true, the space run advances i to 2, text[2]='1' is neither a sign nor CR/DB, so the return is i+1 = 3 — the value the rule names verbatim. Also traced "0  1" -> 4 and "12 34" -> 4 (the first non-space after the run, not the run's start). TEST: conformance:cases/15.90.4-Returned-value-rule/intrinsics_test_validators line 60-61 is the verbatim example, pinned N5=03 in the .out; its source comment cites the sub-note. The half (i) branch is pinned by the same golden's N2/N3 (a trailing space run and a space-then-CR both = 0).

REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; one cited test observation is WRONG and is replaced, and the substituted evidence is stronger): the closing sentence claims half (i) is "pinned by the same golden's N2/N3 (a trailing space run and a space-then-CR both = 0)". N3 is FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL("123cr") — intrinsics_test_validators.cob line 54 — which contains NO SPACE AT ALL; it pins the mixed-case CR of §15.67.3 r1's alphanumeric bullet, not the space-then-CR path. Half (i)'s "spaces then end of string" arm IS pinned, by N2 (" + 12 " = 0, a trailing space run) and, over a DATA ITEM rather than a literal, by conformance:cases/15.67.3-Argument-rules/pb33_numval_family_digit_cap TEST-31 = 0 over `S31 PIC X(44)` whose 32-character value leaves a 12-space padded tail — a case the adjudicator never cited and which is the better witness. Half (i)'s "spaces then a trailing sign/CR-DB" arm has NO test in the corpus; I closed it by reading lines 622 then 630-633 and hand-tracing "12 CR" -> 0, "12 - " -> 0 and "12 -" -> 0. Half (ii) is untouched: the "0 1" -> 3 example is pinned verbatim at N5=03, and I re-traced it and "0  1" -> 4, "12 34" -> 4, "1 .5" -> 3 independently. Both halves stand; only the evidence line is corrected.

[folded RV-15.93.4-L2.2 = §15.93.4 1) b) 2.: CONFORMS]
MECHANICAL TEST-REF REPAIR ONLY — the verdict, its grounds and its editions are UNCHANGED and are not re-litigated here. kb/Work PB256 renamed unit TestNumvalScannerTests.DigitCap_FollowsArithmeticMode to DigitCapParameter_SelectsTheSubNoteVerdict, because the old name asserted a mode selection the test could not reach (it passes the cap as a literal; no arithmetic mode is in scope in a unit test) and SpecTraceabilityInventoryDriftTests.EveryTestRef_ResolvesToARealTest would otherwise go red on a dangling ref. The row's own claim is unaffected: as its note already records, sub-note 2's NATIVE selection is the one arm measured end to end anyway, because DigitCapFlag's native branch is the EMPTY string and conformance:cases/15.90.4-Returned-value-rule/intrinsics_test_validators has no OPTIONS paragraph, so N10 = 32 exercises the selection and the verdict together. conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_mode_flags is added as the two-sided companion: its PB256NAT unit pins the native 32nd-digit verdict (P5 = 32) in the SAME file whose PB256STD unit answers 0 to that identical argument under a standard mode, so the native cap is now measured against a live contrast rather than alone.

[folded RV-15.93.4-L2.3 = §15.93.4 1) b) 3.: DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT]
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.4 "If standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, and the argument has more than 35 digits, the returned value is the position of the 36th digit" -> OK (§15.93.4 rule 1, sub-note 3). THE RULE'S PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER. READ: DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) — `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error("COBOL0806", "ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO §8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL")` — a hard compile error, so no object program can ever run with standard-binary in effect. Correspondingly the 35-digit cap is NOWHERE in the tree: IntrinsicRenderer.DigitCapFlag (line 800) is a two-valued property, `num.StandardDecimal ? ", digitCap: 34" : ""`, and NvScan's parameter takes 31 or 34 and nothing else; the renderer's own comment at line 263 records the omission ("standard-binary's 35 rides the P12/P13 STANDARD-BINARY wave"). So on the code alone this is NOT-IMPLEMENTED. I do not record that verdict, because the established adjudication of the identical shape is an owner question, not a defect: RV-15.27.3-2 (FUNCTION E) and RV-15.73.3-2 (FUNCTION PI) are both open at NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION on exactly this precondition, on the grounds that Annex A.3 item 2 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY processor-dependent, Annex F.2 makes it obsolete, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2 already records the non-support — the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, which decision D13 reserves to the owner; plan §4678 still carries "STANDARD-BINARY (2014 pending row)" as unresolved. BARE QUESTION: should §15.93.4 rule 1 sub-note 3 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence), as proposed for its FUNCTION E / FUNCTION PI siblings, rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? One decision should settle the whole family. EDITIONS derived independently of IntrinsicCatalog: the STANDARD-BINARY alternative of the OPTIONS ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only — the derivation recorded and re-verified on RV-15.27.3-2), so the precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST: none, and none would qualify — the honest cover is a negative fixture pinning that FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE, which does not exist; a mode-only rejection test that never names TEST-NUMVAL would not cover this row.

REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; the two load-bearing claims were the kind a refuter must not take on trust — an INHERITED precedent and an asserted diagnostic — and both check out): (1) The claimed precedent is REAL, not remembered. I read tests/version-matrix/traceability-inventory.json directly: RV-15.27.3-2 (§15.27.3, subject "E function") and RV-15.73.3-2 (§15.73.3, subject "PI function") both carry verdict NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION, editions "2014,2023" and an EMPTY test-ref, and RV-15.27.3-2's note independently records the same COBOL0806 mechanism re-verified on the built CLI. This row's verdict, editions and empty test-ref are consistent with the family, so the adjudicator is not inventing a third disposition. (2) The diagnostic is a hard Error, not a warning: DataBinder.cs:318-320 reads exactly as quoted, `Edition.Error("COBOL0806", ...)`, and the surrounding comment (306-320) confirms the mode is documented-unsupported at EVERY edition that has it. (3) I re-confirmed the absence of any 35 independently: DigitCapFlag is the only producer of a digitCap argument, it is two-valued, and NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal (line 394) resolves to StandardDecimal-or-Standard, never StandardBinary — so no path can pass 35. NOT-IMPLEMENTED would be the code-only verdict, and I considered recording it, but batch rule 6 reserves the documented-non-support disposition to the owner and the sibling rows fix the family's shape; the bare question stands as put. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

[folded RV-15.93.4-L2.4 = §15.93.4 1) b) 4.: CONFORMS]
PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB256, 2026-09-13), with all THREE parts of this record's rule text adjudicated for the first time — sub-note 4, leg c), and leg c)'s NOTE.
(1) LEG c) AND ITS NOTE, the two thirds the refutation found adjudicated NOWHERE, are adjudicated HERE and covered by a golden written for them: conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_leg_c_and_national measures all three NOTE kinds — Z (zero-length literal) = 1, SP (PIC X(4) of spaces) = 5, INC (" +.", the NOTE's VERBATIM example) = 4 — plus two further valid-but-incomplete shapes ("+" = 2, "." = 2, "+ " = 3) and the same leg on the E-form twin. ⛔ The rule's value is an ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION OVER ANOTHER FUNCTION, so the golden measures that arithmetic rather than a constant: LEN pins FUNCTION LENGTH(NSP) = 4 beside NS = 5 on the SAME national item, so 'FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1' is observed at both operands. The 2002 leg-c witness is the older conformance:cases/15.90.4-Returned-value-rule/intrinsics_test_validators (N8 = 5, N9 = 4).
(2) HALF (i), THE MODE SELECTION, HAD NO TEST OF ANY KIND AND NOW HAS AN END-TO-END ONE. conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_standard_decimal compiles TEST-NUMVAL under OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. — the golden the refuter said the row should be closed by — and is DISCRIMINATING rather than merely confirming: NV32 (32 digits) = 0, which only the 34 cap admits and which native answers 32 for, then NV34 = 0 at the boundary and NV35 = 35 at sub-note 4's own verdict. NVDOT adds the shape a character count would get wrong: 25 + 10 = 35 digits around a decimal separator puts the 35th DIGIT at character 36, and the rule names a digit ordinal.
(3) THE ARITHMETIC-IS-STANDARD ARM — the fourth arm of the same selection, which the refutation called an unmeasured precondition widening — is now MEASURED, not merely determined. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD (the COBOL-2002 mode, obsolete 2014, removed 2023) is named by none of §15.93.4's sub-notes; WiseOwl COBOL's recorded determination is that it takes 34 because its standard intermediate data item IS the standard decimal one and it routes to the same engine (ArithmeticModes.NumvalDigitCap, whose remark states it; kb/Work PB194/PB198). conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_mode_flags unit PB256STD measures exactly that: S1 (32 digits) = 0 where the same argument in the file's own native unit answers 32, and S2 (35 digits) = 35.
SUB-NOTE 3's standard-binary 35 belongs to the L2.3 sibling and is the PB198 decline there.
EDITIONS CORRECTED 2014,2023 -> 2002,2014,2023. The prior value was derived from sub-note 4 alone (STANDARD-DECIMAL is a COBOL-2014 addition), but this record's text also carries leg c) and its NOTE, which carry no mode precondition and apply wherever TEST-NUMVAL exists — i.e. from 2002. That is the same under-reading of the record's own text that the refutation's first finding named.
THE UNIT TEST IS RENAMED: DigitCap_FollowsArithmeticMode -> DigitCapParameter_SelectsTheSubNoteVerdict. It passes the cap as a literal and always did; the new name says what it measures (the scan's response to each cap value) and its class remark now points at the goldens that measure the arm left of it. IntrinsicModeFlagCoverageDriftTests keeps that true for any function that gains such an argument later: it derives the (function, flag) pairs from IntrinsicRenderer's own arms crossed with the catalog and fails until an enabled+runnable golden compiles the function under the source construct that turns the flag on. || editions corrected from '85,2002,2014,2023' to 2002,2014,2023 (kb/Work PB3173, S0b; DESIGN-conformance-suite.md §6 step 0): the TEST-NUMVAL function exists from 2002 (IntrinsicCatalog.cs, the COBOL1502 edition window).
